CONFIDENCE: 0.34
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by three intense C-H stretching bands at 2880–2970 cm⁻¹ and a strong C=O stretch at 1736 cm⁻¹, the typical position for a saturated aliphatic ESTER carbonyl.  Peak 1120 cm⁻¹ (strong C–O stretch), together with bands at 963, 894, 867 and 834 cm⁻¹, fit the expected C–O–C and C–C skeletal vibrations of an aliphatic ester containing several CH₃ groups.  Among the candidates, only 1, 7 and 9 are simple aliphatic esters; 6 is an acyl chloride (would give a higher ν(C=O) ≈ 1800 cm⁻¹) and 3/10 are ketones (ν(C=O) ≈ 1715 cm⁻¹).  Candidate 1 (CCOC(=O)CC(C)C, ethyl isovalerate) best explains the pattern: 

• ν(C=O) of ethyl isovalerate is reported near 1735 cm⁻¹, matching the 1736 cm⁻¹ band.  
• Branched isopropyl-like CH₃ groups give three strong ν(CH) bands (2880–2971 cm⁻¹) and a pronounced CH₃/CH₂ scissoring band at 1454 cm⁻¹ (rule GFQ-003).  
• Esters with an ethoxy group show intense C–O stretches near 1120 cm⁻¹, exactly matching the observed 1120 cm⁻¹ peak.  
• Rocking/wagging modes of ethoxy and isobutyl groups appear near 960–900 cm⁻¹ and ~830–880 cm⁻¹, accounting for the 963, 894, 867 and 834 cm⁻¹ bands.  

The overall match of the key ester carbonyl, C–O and aliphatic features makes candidate 1 the most consistent choice with the experimental Raman peaks.
